The PMI framework uses a conditional invertible neural network (cINN) to map noisy observations to the input space.
The cINN consists of a sequence of affine coupling layers.
The real NVP architecture is used in the cINN to explicitly learn the data distribution with exact log-likelihood evaluation.
The PMI framework reduces the design cycle time by enabling explicit inverse design and reducing the need for iterative design processes.
The PMI framework uses a probabilistic approach to handle ill-posed inverse problems.
The PMI framework captures the uncertainty due to the forward process and the epistemic uncertainty due to limited data.
The PMI framework uses a conditioning network to map noisy observations to a conditioning input.

The main challenge in designing gas turbine blades is the need to balance multiple competing objectives.

The PMI framework is demonstrated on the inverse aerodynamic design of a 3D blade of a last stage blade of an industrial gas turbine.
The PMI framework uses a multi-fidelity Gaussian Process (MFGP) to model the forward process.
The PMI framework uses a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to estimate the hyperparameters of the MFGP.
